# Mismatched Dependencies Brick Pool Provisioning
**#214800**
- Severity: Low
- Validity: Unreviewed
## Source locations
### `src/plugin/contracts/CustomPoolPluginFactory.sol` (2 locations)
#### Lines 60-73 — _The initializer stores the factory and entry point without validating their relationship._

```
  function initialize(address _factory, address _algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint, address _pluginImplementation) external initializer {
    require(_factory != address(0));
    require(_algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint != address(0));

    __AccessControlEnumerable_init();
    __Ownable2Step_init();

    factory = _factory;
    algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint = _algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint;
    defaultFeeConfiguration = AdaptiveFee.initialFeeConfiguration();

    _grantRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, msg.sender);
    _grantRole(CUSTOM_POOL_DEPLOYER, msg.sender);
    _setImplementation(_pluginImplementation);
```
⋯
#### Lines 90-103 — _Pool prediction uses `factory`, but deployment is routed through the independently configured entry point._

```
    (address token0, address token1) = _sortTokens(tokenA, tokenB);
    address expectedPool = IAlgebraFactory(factory).computeCustomPoolAddress(address(this), token0, token1);
    require(_pendingCustomPoolByAddress[expectedPool].creator == address(0), 'Pool creation pending');

    _pendingCustomPoolByAddress[expectedPool] = PendingCustomPool({
      creator: msg.sender,
      token0: token0,
      token1: token1,
      plugin: address(0),
      dataHash: keccak256(data)
    });

    customPool = IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).createCustomPool(address(this), msg.sender, tokenA, tokenB, data);
    require(customPool == expectedPool, 'Invalid custom pool');
```
### `src/periphery/contracts/AlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint.sol`
#### Lines 27-44 — _The entry point binds creation to its own immutable factory._

```
    constructor(address _factory) {
        require(_factory != address(0));
        factory = _factory;
    }

    /// @inheritdoc IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint
    function createCustomPool(
        address deployer,
        address creator,
        address tokenA,
        address tokenB,
        bytes calldata data
    ) external override returns (address customPool) {
        require(msg.sender == deployer, 'Only deployer');
        if (!isPublicPoolCreationMode) {
            require(isCustomPoolDeployer[deployer], 'Can`t create custom pools');
        }
        return IAlgebraFactory(factory).createCustomPool(deployer, creator, tokenA, tokenB, data);
```
## Description

`initialize` independently accepts nonzero `_factory` and `_algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint` addresses but never verifies that the entry point is configured for that same factory. The two values jointly describe one provisioning route: this contract predicts a pool through `factory`, while `deployCustomPool` sends creation through `algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint`. The entry point forwards creation and authenticates hooks against its own immutable factory, so a mismatch makes the pending record use a different predicted address from the one supplied to the before hook. Because neither dependency has a setter, a misconfigured proxy cannot provision custom pools without a contract upgrade.
## Root cause

The initializer does not cross-validate that `IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(_algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).factory()` equals `_factory`, despite both addresses composing one immutable provisioning route.
## Impact

A configuration mismatch permanently disables custom-pool creation for the proxy's current implementation. Recovery requires upgrading or replacing the factory rather than correcting the stored dependency addresses through normal administration.
## Proof of concept
### Test case

```
import { ethers } from 'hardhat';
import { loadFixture } from '@nomicfoundation/hardhat-network-helpers';
import {
  abi as POOL_DEPLOYER_ABI,
  bytecode as POOL_DEPLOYER_BYTECODE,
} from '@cryptoalgebra/integral-core/artifacts/contracts/AlgebraPoolDeployer.sol/AlgebraPoolDeployer.json';
import {
  abi as ENTRY_POINT_ABI,
  bytecode as ENTRY_POINT_BYTECODE,
} from '@cryptoalgebra/integral-periphery/artifacts/contracts/AlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint.sol/AlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint.json';
import {
  abi as PROXY_ADMIN_ABI,
  bytecode as PROXY_ADMIN_BYTECODE,
} from '@cryptoalgebra/integral-core/artifacts/@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/transparent/ProxyAdmin.sol/ProxyAdmin.json';
import { AlgebraFactoryUpgradeable } from '@cryptoalgebra/integral-core/typechain';
import { CustomPoolPluginFactory } from '../typechain';
import { expect } from './shared/expect';
import { createEmptyFactoryProxy } from './shared/externalFixtures';

const transparentUpgradeableProxyArtifact = require(
  '@cryptoalgebra/integral-core/artifacts/@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/transparent/' +
    'TransparentUpgradeableProxy.sol/TransparentUpgradeableProxy.json'
);
const { abi: TransparentUpgradeableProxy_ABI, bytecode: TransparentUpgradeableProxy_BYTECODE } = transparentUpgradeableProxyArtifact;

const TOKEN_A = '0x1000000000000000000000000000000000000000';
const TOKEN_B = '0x2000000000000000000000000000000000000000';

function sortTokens(tokenA: string, tokenB: string): [string, string] {
  return BigInt(tokenA) < BigInt(tokenB) ? [tokenA, tokenB] : [tokenB, tokenA];
}

describe('PoC mismatched CustomPoolPluginFactory dependencies', () => {
  async function deployInitializedFactory(): Promise<AlgebraFactoryUpgradeable> {
    const factory = await createEmptyFactoryProxy();
    const poolDeployerFactory = await ethers.getContractFactory(POOL_DEPLOYER_ABI, POOL_DEPLOYER_BYTECODE);
    const poolDeployer = await poolDeployerFactory.deploy(factory);
    await factory.initialize(poolDeployer);
    return factory;
  }

  async function deployEmptyCustomPluginFactory(): Promise<CustomPoolPluginFactory> {
    const customFactoryImplementation = await (await ethers.getContractFactory('CustomPoolPluginFactory')).deploy();
    const proxyAdmin = await (await ethers.getContractFactory(PROXY_ADMIN_ABI, PROXY_ADMIN_BYTECODE)).deploy();
    const proxyFactory = await ethers.getContractFactory(TransparentUpgradeableProxy_ABI, TransparentUpgradeableProxy_BYTECODE);
    const proxy = await proxyFactory.deploy(customFactoryImplementation.target, proxyAdmin.target, '0x');
    return (await ethers.getContractAt('CustomPoolPluginFactory', proxy.target)) as any as CustomPoolPluginFactory;
  }

  async function fixture() {
    const factoryRecordedByPlugin = await deployInitializedFactory();
    const factoryUsedByEntryPoint = await deployInitializedFactory();

    const entryPointFactory = await ethers.getContractFactory(ENTRY_POINT_ABI, ENTRY_POINT_BYTECODE);
    const entryPoint = await entryPointFactory.deploy(factoryUsedByEntryPoint);
    await factoryUsedByEntryPoint.grantRole(await factoryUsedByEntryPoint.CUSTOM_POOL_DEPLOYER(), entryPoint);
    await factoryUsedByEntryPoint.grantRole(await factoryUsedByEntryPoint.POOLS_ADMINISTRATOR_ROLE(), entryPoint);

    const pluginImplementation = await (await ethers.getContractFactory('AlgebraBasePluginV1')).deploy();
    const mismatchedCustomFactory = await deployEmptyCustomPluginFactory();

    // Vulnerable initializer: accepts individually nonzero but mutually inconsistent dependencies.
    await mismatchedCustomFactory.initialize(factoryRecordedByPlugin, entryPoint, pluginImplementation);
    await entryPoint.setCustomPoolDeployer(await mismatchedCustomFactory.getAddress(), true);
    await mismatchedCustomFactory.setTokenWhitelistBatch([TOKEN_A, TOKEN_B], true);

    // Control instance on the same entry point proves the role/whitelist/deployer path is otherwise usable.
    const healthyCustomFactory = await deployEmptyCustomPluginFactory();
    await healthyCustomFactory.initialize(factoryUsedByEntryPoint, entryPoint, pluginImplementation);
    await entryPoint.setCustomPoolDeployer(await healthyCustomFactory.getAddress(), true);
    await healthyCustomFactory.setTokenWhitelistBatch([TOKEN_A, TOKEN_B], true);

    return { factoryRecordedByPlugin, factoryUsedByEntryPoint, entryPoint, mismatchedCustomFactory, healthyCustomFactory };
  }

  it('accepts an entry point bound to another factory and then bricks custom pool provisioning', async () => {
    const { factoryRecordedByPlugin, factoryUsedByEntryPoint, entryPoint, mismatchedCustomFactory, healthyCustomFactory } = await loadFixture(
      fixture
    );
    const [token0, token1] = sortTokens(TOKEN_A, TOKEN_B);

    expect(await mismatchedCustomFactory.factory()).to.eq(await factoryRecordedByPlugin.getAddress());
    expect(await mismatchedCustomFactory.algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint()).to.eq(await entryPoint.getAddress());
    expect(await entryPoint.factory()).to.eq(await factoryUsedByEntryPoint.getAddress());
    expect(await mismatchedCustomFactory.factory()).to.not.eq(await entryPoint.factory());

    const wronglyPredictedPool = await factoryRecordedByPlugin.computeCustomPoolAddress(await mismatchedCustomFactory.getAddress(), token0, token1);
    const poolThatEntryPointWillAskHooksFor = await factoryUsedByEntryPoint.computeCustomPoolAddress(
      await mismatchedCustomFactory.getAddress(),
      token0,
      token1
    );
    expect(wronglyPredictedPool).to.not.eq(poolThatEntryPointWillAskHooksFor);

    await expect(mismatchedCustomFactory.deployCustomPool(TOKEN_B, TOKEN_A, '0x1234')).to.be.revertedWith('Invalid creator');
    expect(await mismatchedCustomFactory.isCustomPool(wronglyPredictedPool)).to.eq(false);
    expect(await mismatchedCustomFactory.isCustomPool(poolThatEntryPointWillAskHooksFor)).to.eq(false);

    const healthyPool = await factoryUsedByEntryPoint.computeCustomPoolAddress(await healthyCustomFactory.getAddress(), token0, token1);
    await expect(healthyCustomFactory.deployCustomPool(TOKEN_B, TOKEN_A, '0x1234')).to.emit(factoryUsedByEntryPoint, 'CustomPool');
    expect(await healthyCustomFactory.isCustomPool(healthyPool)).to.eq(true);
  });
});
```

### Considerations

PoC demonstrates the deployment/configuration defect through real Hardhat execution of CustomPoolPluginFactory.initialize(), CustomPoolPluginFactory.deployCustomPool(), AlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint.createCustomPool(), and AlgebraFactoryUpgradeable.createCustomPool(). It models an operator/proxy initialization misconfiguration, not an external attacker changing dependencies after initialization. The test asserts the mismatched dependency state, the divergent predicted pool addresses, the deployCustomPool revert at the real before-hook lookup, and a correctly wired control deployment succeeding under the same entry point/factory roles.
### Validation reasoning

PoC validation command completed successfully.
## Remediation
### Explanation

The initializer now verifies that the configured custom-pool entry point is bound to the same Algebra factory before storing either dependency, preventing an irreparable mismatched provisioning route.
### Patch

```diff
diff --git a/src/plugin/contracts/CustomPoolPluginFactory.sol b/src/plugin/contracts/CustomPoolPluginFactory.sol
--- a/src/plugin/contracts/CustomPoolPluginFactory.sol
+++ b/src/plugin/contracts/CustomPoolPluginFactory.sol
@@ -1,247 +1,248 @@
 // SPDX-License-Identifier: BUSL-1.1
 pragma solidity =0.8.20;
 
 import '@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/beacon/BeaconProxy.sol';
 import '@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/access/AccessControlEnumerableUpgradeable.sol';
 import '@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/access/Ownable2StepUpgradeable.sol';
 
 import '@cryptoalgebra/integral-core/contracts/interfaces/IAlgebraFactory.sol';
 import '@cryptoalgebra/integral-periphery/contracts/interfaces/IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint.sol';
 
 import './interfaces/IAlgebraBasePluginV1.sol';
 import './interfaces/ICustomPoolPluginFactory.sol';
 import './libraries/AdaptiveFee.sol';
 
 /// @title Algebra custom pool plugin factory
 /// @dev This contract is an edited copy of BasePluginV1Factory created for custom pools logic.
 /// @notice Entry point for custom pool creation and custom pool plugin deployment.
 contract CustomPoolPluginFactory is ICustomPoolPluginFactory, AccessControlEnumerableUpgradeable, Ownable2StepUpgradeable {
   /// @notice Role that can deploy custom pools when public creation mode is disabled.
   bytes32 public constant override CUSTOM_POOL_DEPLOYER = keccak256('CUSTOM_POOL_DEPLOYER');
 
   /// @notice Algebra factory used for custom pool deployment.
   address public override factory;
 
   /// @notice Algebra custom pool entry point used to create and manage custom pools.
   address public override algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint;
 
   /// @notice Whether custom pool creation is public.
   bool public override isPublicPoolCreationMode;
 
   /// @notice Current default dynamic fee configuration for newly created plugins.
   AlgebraFeeConfiguration public override defaultFeeConfiguration;
 
   /// @inheritdoc IBeacon
   address public override implementation;
 
   /// @notice Plugin created for each custom pool.
   mapping(address pool => address plugin) public override pluginByPool;
 
   /// @notice Whether a token can be used for custom pool creation.
   mapping(address token => bool allowed) public override isWhitelistedToken;
 
   /// @notice Whether a pool was created through this factory.
   mapping(address pool => bool allowed) public override isCustomPool;
 
   struct PendingCustomPool {
     address creator;
     address token0;
     address token1;
     address plugin;
     bytes32 dataHash;
   }
 
   mapping(address pool => PendingCustomPool pendingCustomPool) private _pendingCustomPoolByAddress;
 
   constructor() {
     _disableInitializers();
   }
 
   function initialize(address _factory, address _algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint, address _pluginImplementation) external initializer {
     require(_factory != address(0));
     require(_algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint != address(0));
+    require(IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(_algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).factory() == _factory, 'Invalid entry point');
 
     __AccessControlEnumerable_init();
     __Ownable2Step_init();
 
     factory = _factory;
     algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint = _algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint;
     defaultFeeConfiguration = AdaptiveFee.initialFeeConfiguration();
 
     _grantRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, msg.sender);
     _grantRole(CUSTOM_POOL_DEPLOYER, msg.sender);
     _setImplementation(_pluginImplementation);
 
     emit DefaultFeeConfiguration(defaultFeeConfiguration);
   }
 
   /// @notice Deploys a custom pool with a newly created default plugin.
   /// @param tokenA One token from the pair.
   /// @param tokenB The other token from the pair.
   /// @param data Additional plugin creation data.
   /// @return customPool The newly created custom pool.
   function deployCustomPool(address tokenA, address tokenB, bytes calldata data) external returns (address customPool) {
     if (!isPublicPoolCreationMode) {
       _checkRole(CUSTOM_POOL_DEPLOYER);
     }
     require(isWhitelistedToken[tokenA], 'TokenA not whitelisted');
     require(isWhitelistedToken[tokenB], 'TokenB not whitelisted');
 
     (address token0, address token1) = _sortTokens(tokenA, tokenB);
     address expectedPool = IAlgebraFactory(factory).computeCustomPoolAddress(address(this), token0, token1);
     require(_pendingCustomPoolByAddress[expectedPool].creator == address(0), 'Pool creation pending');
 
     _pendingCustomPoolByAddress[expectedPool] = PendingCustomPool({
       creator: msg.sender,
       token0: token0,
       token1: token1,
       plugin: address(0),
       dataHash: keccak256(data)
     });
 
     customPool = IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).createCustomPool(address(this), msg.sender, tokenA, tokenB, data);
     require(customPool == expectedPool, 'Invalid custom pool');
     require(isCustomPool[customPool], 'Custom pool hook missing');
   }
 
   /// @inheritdoc IAlgebraPluginFactory
   function createPlugin(address, address, address) external pure override returns (address) {
     revert('Deprecated');
   }
 
   /// @inheritdoc IAlgebraPluginFactory
   function beforeCreatePoolHook(
     address pool,
     address creator,
     address deployer,
     address token0,
     address token1,
     bytes calldata data
   ) external override returns (address plugin) {
     require(msg.sender == algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint, 'Only entry point');
     require(deployer == address(this), 'Invalid deployer');
 
     PendingCustomPool storage pendingCustomPool = _pendingCustomPoolByAddress[pool];
     require(pendingCustomPool.creator == creator, 'Invalid creator');
     require(pendingCustomPool.token0 == token0 && pendingCustomPool.token1 == token1, 'Invalid tokens');
     require(pendingCustomPool.dataHash == keccak256(data), 'Invalid data');
 
     plugin = _createPlugin(pool);
     pendingCustomPool.plugin = plugin;
   }
 
   /// @inheritdoc IAlgebraPluginFactory
   function afterCreatePoolHook(address plugin, address pool, address deployer) external override {
     require(msg.sender == algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint, 'Only entry point');
     require(deployer == address(this), 'Invalid deployer');
 
     PendingCustomPool storage pendingCustomPool = _pendingCustomPoolByAddress[pool];
     require(pendingCustomPool.creator != address(0), 'Pool not pending');
     require(pendingCustomPool.plugin == plugin, 'Invalid plugin');
     require(pluginByPool[pool] == plugin, 'Plugin not created');
 
     delete _pendingCustomPoolByAddress[pool];
     isCustomPool[pool] = true;
   }
 
   /// @notice Changes tick spacing in a custom pool created by this factory.
   function setTickSpacing(address pool, int24 newTickSpacing) external onlyOwner {
     _checkCustomPool(pool);
     IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).setTickSpacing(pool, newTickSpacing);
   }
 
   /// @notice Changes plugin address in a custom pool created by this factory.
   function setPlugin(address pool, address newPluginAddress) external onlyOwner {
     _checkCustomPool(pool);
     IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).setPlugin(pool, newPluginAddress);
   }
 
   /// @notice Changes plugin config in a custom pool created by this factory.
   function setPluginConfig(address pool, uint8 newConfig) external onlyOwner {
     _checkCustomPool(pool);
     IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).setPluginConfig(pool, newConfig);
   }
 
   /// @notice Changes fee in a custom pool created by this factory.
   function setFee(address pool, uint16 newFee) external onlyOwner {
     _checkCustomPool(pool);
     IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).setFee(pool, newFee);
   }
 
   /// @notice Changes public custom pool creation mode.
   function setPublicPoolCreationMode(bool mode) external onlyOwner {
     require(isPublicPoolCreationMode != mode);
     isPublicPoolCreationMode = mode;
     emit PublicPoolCreationMode(mode);
   }
 
   /// @notice Changes a token whitelist status.
   function setTokenWhitelist(address token, bool allowed) external onlyOwner {
     _setTokenWhitelist(token, allowed);
   }
 
   /// @notice Changes whitelist status for a batch of tokens.
   function setTokenWhitelistBatch(address[] calldata tokens, bool allowed) external onlyOwner {
     uint256 tokensLength = tokens.length;
     for (uint256 i; i < tokensLength; ++i) {
       _setTokenWhitelist(tokens[i], allowed);
     }
   }
 
   /// @notice Changes initial fee configuration for new plugins.
   function setDefaultFeeConfiguration(AlgebraFeeConfiguration calldata newConfig) external onlyOwner {
     AdaptiveFee.validateFeeConfiguration(newConfig);
     defaultFeeConfiguration = newConfig;
     emit DefaultFeeConfiguration(newConfig);
   }
 
   /// @notice Upgrades the beacon to a new implementation.
   function upgradeTo(address newImplementation) external onlyOwner {
     _setImplementation(newImplementation);
   }
 
   function _createPlugin(address pool) internal returns (address plugin) {
     require(pluginByPool[pool] == address(0), 'Already created');
     IAlgebraBasePluginV1 customPoolPlugin = IAlgebraBasePluginV1(address(new BeaconProxy(address(this), '')));
     customPoolPlugin.initialize(pool, factory, address(this));
     customPoolPlugin.changeFeeConfiguration(defaultFeeConfiguration);
     plugin = address(customPoolPlugin);
     pluginByPool[pool] = plugin;
   }
 
   function _setTokenWhitelist(address token, bool allowed) internal {
     require(token != address(0));
     require(isWhitelistedToken[token] != allowed);
     isWhitelistedToken[token] = allowed;
     emit TokenWhitelist(token, allowed);
   }
 
   function _setImplementation(address newImplementation) internal {
     if (newImplementation.code.length == 0) {
       revert BeaconInvalidImplementation(newImplementation);
     }
     implementation = newImplementation;
     emit Upgraded(newImplementation);
   }
 
   function _checkCustomPool(address pool) internal view {
     require(isCustomPool[pool], 'Unknown custom pool');
   }
 
   function _sortTokens(address tokenA, address tokenB) internal pure returns (address token0, address token1) {
     require(tokenA != tokenB);
     (token0, token1) = tokenA < tokenB ? (tokenA, tokenB) : (tokenB, tokenA);
     require(token0 != address(0));
   }
 
   /// @dev Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account.
   function _transferOwnership(address newOwner) internal override {
     _revokeRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, owner());
     super._transferOwnership(newOwner);
     if (owner() != address(0)) {
       _grantRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, owner());
     }
   }
 
   uint256[50] private __gap;
 }
```

# Front-run permits can revert bundled migrations
**#214816**
- Severity: Low
- Validity: Unreviewed
## Source locations
### `src/periphery/contracts/V3Migrator.sol`
#### Lines 44-50 — _The subsequent migration relies on the current caller as the LP owner, so a consumed permit prevents the intended migration rather than authorizing the front-runner._

### `src/periphery/contracts/interfaces/ISelfPermit.sol`
#### Lines 15-40 — _The interface exposes both the ordinary and conditional EIP-2612 variants for multicall use._

```
    function selfPermit(
        address token,
        uint256 value,
        uint256 deadline,
        uint8 v,
        bytes32 r,
        bytes32 s
    ) external payable;

    /// @notice Permits this contract to spend a given token from `msg.sender`
    /// @dev The `owner` is always msg.sender and the `spender` is always address(this).
    /// Can be used instead of #selfPermit to prevent calls from failing due to a frontrun of a call to #selfPermit
    /// @param token The address of the token spent
    /// @param value The amount that can be spent of token
    /// @param deadline A timestamp, the current blocktime must be less than or equal to this timestamp
    /// @param v Must produce valid secp256k1 signature from the holder along with `r` and `s`
    /// @param r Must produce valid secp256k1 signature from the holder along with `v` and `s`
    /// @param s Must produce valid secp256k1 signature from the holder along with `r` and `v`
    function selfPermitIfNecessary(
        address token,
        uint256 value,
        uint256 deadline,
        uint8 v,
        bytes32 r,
        bytes32 s
    ) external payable;
```
## Description

The public `selfPermit` helper accepts a standalone EIP-2612 signature that grants this contract an allowance from `msg.sender`. A user can place this call before `migrate` in `multicall`, but the signature is not bound to that migration payload. A mempool observer can submit the same permit first, consuming its nonce while setting the intended allowance. The user's batched `selfPermit` then fails because the nonce has been consumed, and `multicall` bubbles that failure so `migrate` never executes. `selfPermitIfNecessary` avoids this outcome only when the allowance already satisfies `value`; batches using the ordinary helper remain susceptible.
## Root cause

`selfPermit` exposes a replayable-in-the-mempool, nonce-consuming authorization that is not conditionally skipped or atomically bound to the subsequent action.
## Impact

An observer can repeatedly cause a user's bundled migration transaction to revert by front-running each newly signed permit, forcing the user to acquire another signature and resubmit. The copied authorization does not let the observer migrate the user's LP tokens because `migrate` transfers liquidity from the current `msg.sender`, so the demonstrated effect is denial of the intended transaction.
## Proof of concept
### Test case

```
import { MaxUint256, Wallet } from 'ethers';
import { ethers } from 'hardhat';
import { loadFixture } from '@nomicfoundation/hardhat-network-helpers';
import { abi as PAIR_V2_ABI } from '@uniswap/v2-core/build/UniswapV2Pair.json';

import completeFixture from './shared/completeFixture';
import { v2FactoryFixture } from './shared/externalFixtures';
import { encodePriceSqrt } from './shared/encodePriceSqrt';
import { getPermitSignature } from './shared/permit';
import { sortedTokens } from './shared/tokenSort';
import { getMaxTick, getMinTick } from './shared/ticks';
import { expect } from './shared/expect';
import { IUniswapV2Pair, MockTimeNonfungiblePositionManager, TestERC20, V3Migrator, IWNativeToken } from '../typechain';


type TestERC20WithAddress = TestERC20 & { address: string | undefined };

describe('PoC: front-run selfPermit reverts a bundled V3 migration', function () {
  this.timeout(40_000);

  async function fixture(): Promise<{
    wallet: Wallet;
    attacker: Wallet;
    token: TestERC20WithAddress;
    wnative: IWNativeToken;
    nft: MockTimeNonfungiblePositionManager;
    migrator: V3Migrator;
    pair: IUniswapV2Pair;
    expectedLiquidity: bigint;
    tokenLower: boolean;
  }> {
    const [wallet, attacker] = (await (ethers as any).getSigners()) as Wallet[];
    const { factory, tokens, nft, wnative } = await completeFixture();
    const { factory: factoryV2 } = await v2FactoryFixture();

    const token = tokens[0] as TestERC20WithAddress;
    token.address = await token.getAddress();

    await wnative.deposit({ value: 10_000 });
    await factoryV2.createPair(await token.getAddress(), await wnative.getAddress());
    const pairAddress = await factoryV2.getPair(await token.getAddress(), await wnative.getAddress());
    const pair = new ethers.Contract(pairAddress, PAIR_V2_ABI, wallet) as any as IUniswapV2Pair;

    await token.transfer(pairAddress, 10_000);
    await wnative.transfer(pairAddress, 10_000);
    await pair.mint(wallet.address);

    const [token0, token1] = await sortedTokens(wnative, token);
    const migrator = (await (await ethers.getContractFactory('V3Migrator')).deploy(
      factory,
      wnative,
      nft,
      await factory.poolDeployer()
    )) as any as V3Migrator;
    await migrator.createAndInitializePoolIfNecessary(token0, token1, encodePriceSqrt(1, 1));

    return {
      wallet,
      attacker,
      token,
      wnative,
      nft,
      migrator,
      pair,
      expectedLiquidity: 9_000n,
      tokenLower: (await wnative.getAddress()) > (await token.getAddress()),
    };
  }

  it('uses a copied LP-token permit to consume the nonce, then the victim multicall reverts before migrate', async () => {
    const { wallet, attacker, token, wnative, nft, migrator, pair, expectedLiquidity, tokenLower } = await loadFixture(
      fixture
    );

    const pairAddress = await pair.getAddress();
    const migratorAddress = await migrator.getAddress();
    const deadline = MaxUint256;

    const { v, r, s } = await getPermitSignature(wallet, pair as any, migratorAddress, expectedLiquidity, deadline);

    const migrateParams = {
      pair: pairAddress,
      liquidityToMigrate: expectedLiquidity,
      percentageToMigrate: 100,
      token0: tokenLower ? await token.getAddress() : await wnative.getAddress(),
      token1: tokenLower ? await wnative.getAddress() : await token.getAddress(),
      tickLower: getMinTick(60),
      tickUpper: getMaxTick(60),
      amount0Min: 9_000,
      amount1Min: 9_000,
      recipient: wallet.address,
      deadline: 1,
      refundAsNative: false,
    };

    const vulnerableBatch = [
      migrator.interface.encodeFunctionData('selfPermit', [pairAddress, expectedLiquidity, deadline, v, r, s]),
      migrator.interface.encodeFunctionData('migrate', [migrateParams]),
    ];

    // Baseline: without the attacker transaction, the user's ordinary selfPermit + migrate multicall succeeds.
    await migrator.multicall.staticCall(vulnerableBatch);

    expect(await pair.nonces(wallet.address)).to.equal(0);
    expect(await pair.allowance(wallet.address, migratorAddress)).to.equal(0);
    expect(await nft.balanceOf(wallet.address)).to.equal(0);

    // Anyone can submit the same standalone permit first. It consumes the LP-token nonce and grants the intended allowance
    // to the real V3Migrator, but does not execute migrate because V3Migrator.migrate pulls LP tokens from msg.sender.
    await pair.connect(attacker).permit(wallet.address, migratorAddress, expectedLiquidity, deadline, v, r, s);
    expect(await pair.nonces(wallet.address)).to.equal(1);
    expect(await pair.allowance(wallet.address, migratorAddress)).to.equal(expectedLiquidity);
    expect(await pair.balanceOf(wallet.address)).to.equal(expectedLiquidity);

    await expect(migrator.multicall(vulnerableBatch)).to.be.reverted;

    // The multicall's reverted selfPermit prevented the later delegatecalled migrate from running.
    expect(await nft.balanceOf(wallet.address)).to.equal(0);
    expect(await pair.balanceOf(wallet.address)).to.equal(expectedLiquidity);

    // The consumed permit only caused denial of the bundled transaction. With the allowance already set, migrate itself
    // still succeeds when the victim sends a separate transaction, proving the blocked subcall was the real migration path.
    await migrator.migrate(migrateParams);
    expect(await nft.balanceOf(wallet.address)).to.equal(1);
    const position = await nft.positions(1);
    expect(position.liquidity).to.be.gt(0);
    expect(await pair.balanceOf(wallet.address)).to.equal(0);
  });
});
```

### Considerations

PoC executed successfully in the periphery Hardhat harness (`unit:cryptoalgebra-integral-periphery`) against the real `V3Migrator`, `SelfPermit`, `Multicall`, and Uniswap V2 pair permit code. It models ordering by submitting the copied permit before the victim multicall in the same local chain rather than using a live mempool. The test proves denial of the bundled migration: the nonce-consuming permit leaves allowance in place, the victim `multicall([selfPermit, migrate])` reverts before `migrate`, no NFT position is minted, and the same `migrate` succeeds afterward as a separate transaction using the already-created allowance.
### Validation reasoning

PoC validation command completed successfully.
## Remediation
### Explanation

Make the ordinary EIP-2612 selfPermit idempotent when the required allowance is already present, so a front-run permit that consumes the signature nonce no longer reverts the victim's multicall and the subsequent migration can execute.
### Patch

```diff
diff --git a/src/periphery/contracts/base/SelfPermit.sol b/src/periphery/contracts/base/SelfPermit.sol
--- a/src/periphery/contracts/base/SelfPermit.sol
+++ b/src/periphery/contracts/base/SelfPermit.sol
@@ -1,66 +1,66 @@

 pragma solidity >=0.5.0;
 
 import '@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol';
 import '@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/draft-IERC20Permit.sol';
 
 import '../interfaces/ISelfPermit.sol';
 import '../interfaces/external/IERC20PermitAllowed.sol';
 
 /// @title Self Permit
 /// @notice Functionality to call permit on any EIP-2612-compliant token for use in the route
 /// @dev These functions are expected to be embedded in multicalls to allow EOAs to approve a contract and call a function
 /// that requires an approval in a single transaction.
 abstract contract SelfPermit is ISelfPermit {
     /// @inheritdoc ISelfPermit
     function selfPermit(
         address token,
         uint256 value,
         uint256 deadline,
         uint8 v,
         bytes32 r,
         bytes32 s
     ) public payable override {
-        IERC20Permit(token).permit(msg.sender, address(this), value, deadline, v, r, s);
+        if (_getAllowance(token) < value) IERC20Permit(token).permit(msg.sender, address(this), value, deadline, v, r, s);
     }
 
     /// @inheritdoc ISelfPermit
     function selfPermitIfNecessary(
         address token,
         uint256 value,
         uint256 deadline,
         uint8 v,
         bytes32 r,
         bytes32 s
     ) external payable override {
         if (_getAllowance(token) < value) selfPermit(token, value, deadline, v, r, s);
     }
 
     /// @inheritdoc ISelfPermit
     function selfPermitAllowed(
         address token,
         uint256 nonce,
         uint256 expiry,
         uint8 v,
         bytes32 r,
         bytes32 s
     ) public payable override {
         IERC20PermitAllowed(token).permit(msg.sender, address(this), nonce, expiry, true, v, r, s);
     }
 
     /// @inheritdoc ISelfPermit
     function selfPermitAllowedIfNecessary(
         address token,
         uint256 nonce,
         uint256 expiry,
         uint8 v,
         bytes32 r,
         bytes32 s
     ) external payable override {
         if (_getAllowance(token) < type(uint256).max) selfPermitAllowed(token, nonce, expiry, v, r, s);
     }
 
     function _getAllowance(address token) private view returns (uint256) {
         return IERC20(token).allowance(msg.sender, address(this));
     }
 }
```

## Description

The swap loop calculates the community portion of each individual `step.feeAmount` as `floor(step.feeAmount * communityFee / COMMUNITY_FEE_DENOMINATOR)`. It subtracts only that floored `delta` from the step fee and credits the remainder to `totalFeeGrowthInput`, while accumulating only `delta` in `communityFeeAmount`. Because price movement is split at initialized ticks, a multi-tick swap performs this truncating calculation repeatedly instead of applying the configured share to the aggregate fee. The sum of the per-step floors can therefore be less than the floor of the aggregate community-fee entitlement, and `_changeReserves` receives the already-understated accumulated amount. Liquidity can be fragmented across initialized boundaries to increase the number of rounding opportunities, causing the retained dust to accrue to LP fee growth rather than the community recipient.
## Root cause

`SwapCalculation` floors the community-fee calculation separately for every swap step without carrying fractional remainders or reconciling against the aggregate swap fee.
## Impact

The community vault receives less than its configured share of swap fees, while the omitted fractional amounts remain available to liquidity providers through fee growth. Each affected step loses less than one smallest token unit, but repeated swaps over many initialized ticks can accumulate this revenue leakage.
## Proof of concept
### Test case

```
import { ethers } from 'hardhat';
import { loadFixture } from '@nomicfoundation/hardhat-network-helpers';

import { expect } from './shared/expect';
import { poolFixture } from './shared/fixtures';
import { createPoolFunctions, encodePriceSqrt, MaxUint128 } from './shared/utilities';

const COMMUNITY_FEE_DENOMINATOR = 1000n;

async function collectableToken0Fees(pool: any, owner: string, ranges: Array<[number, number]>): Promise<bigint> {
  let total = 0n;
  for (const [bottomTick, topTick] of ranges) {
    await pool.burn(bottomTick, topTick, 0, '0x');
    const { amount0 } = await pool.collect.staticCall(owner, bottomTick, topTick, MaxUint128, MaxUint128);
    total += amount0;
  }
  return total;
}

describe('PoC: per-step community fee rounding', () => {
  it('leaves crossed-step community-fee dust in LP-collectable swap fees', async () => {
    const [wallet] = await ethers.getSigners();
    const { token0, token1, swapTargetCallee, createPool } = await loadFixture(poolFixture);
    const pool = await createPool();
    const { mint, swapExact0For1 } = createPoolFunctions({ token0, token1, swapTarget: swapTargetCallee, pool });

    await pool.initialize(encodePriceSqrt(1, 1));

    // Configure a real pool so each small per-step fee is almost entirely owed to the community.
    // With communityFee=999/1000, a safe aggregate calculation would keep at most 1/1000 of swap fees for LPs.
    await pool.setFee(1);
    await pool.setCommunityFee(999);

    const ranges: Array<[number, number]> = [];
    const fullRange: [number, number] = [-600, 600];
    ranges.push(fullRange);
    await mint(wallet.address, fullRange[0], fullRange[1], 1_000_000n);

    // Permissionless LP fragmentation initializes many boundaries that split one economic swap into many steps.
    for (let tick = -600; tick < 0; tick += 60) {
      const range: [number, number] = [tick, tick + 60];
      ranges.push(range);
      await mint(wallet.address, range[0], range[1], 1n);
    }

    const vaultBefore = await token0.balanceOf(await pool.communityVault());
    const [pending0Before] = await pool.getCommunityFeePending();

    const limitPrice = await swapTargetCallee.getPriceAtTick(-600);
    await swapExact0For1(100_000n, wallet.address, limitPrice);

    const vaultAfter = await token0.balanceOf(await pool.communityVault());
    const [pending0After] = await pool.getCommunityFeePending();
    const actualCommunityFee = (vaultAfter - vaultBefore) + (pending0After - pending0Before);

    const lpCollectableToken0 = await collectableToken0Fees(pool, wallet.address, ranges);
    const observedDistributedFees = actualCommunityFee + lpCollectableToken0;
    const aggregateCommunityEntitlement = (observedDistributedFees * 999n) / COMMUNITY_FEE_DENOMINATOR;

    // This assertion is derived from on-chain post-swap state: the pool allocated less to the community than
    // applying the configured 999/1000 share once to the same observed fee pool.
    expect(actualCommunityFee).to.be.lt(aggregateCommunityEntitlement);

    // The leaked units remain in LP accounting: LPs can collect more than the aggregate-safe residual.
    expect(lpCollectableToken0).to.be.gt(observedDistributedFees - aggregateCommunityEntitlement);
  });
});
```

### Considerations

PoC executed successfully in the core Hardhat harness (`unit:cryptoalgebra-integral-core`) and calls the real `AlgebraPool.swap` path through `TestAlgebraCallee`, which reaches `SwapCalculation._calculateSwap` and `ReservesManager._changeReserves`. The test configures a low swap fee and 999/1000 community fee, fragments liquidity across initialized 60-tick boundaries, performs one public exact-input swap across those boundaries, then derives the community allocation and LP-collectable token0 fees from post-swap contract state. It asserts the actual community allocation is below the aggregate community entitlement for the same observed fee pool and that the shortfall is LP-collectable. The PoC does not quantify long-run economic materiality on a production deployment; it demonstrates the per-swap rounding leakage mechanism and state-level impact.
### Validation reasoning

PoC validation command completed successfully.
## Remediation
### Explanation

Carries the fractional community-fee numerator across swap steps, so cumulative deductions equal floor(total swap fees × configured community share / denominator) instead of summing independently rounded-down per-step deductions.
### Patch


## Description

`_blockTimestamp()` intentionally returns a wrapping `uint32` timestamp, and `_distributeRewards()` correctly derives elapsed time through unchecked modular subtraction. In contrast, `applyLiquidityDeltaToPosition()` calls `_distributeRewards()` only when `_blockTimestamp() > _prevTimestamp`. Immediately after the `uint32` clock wraps, this ordinary comparison is false despite time having elapsed, so a liquidity change proceeds without settling rewards against the pre-change `currentLiquidity`. A later distribution calculates the skipped interval with the modified liquidity set, while farming entry can record a reward-growth baseline after that change. The reward checkpoint must use the same modulo-aware elapsed-time semantics as distribution, ensuring every liquidity change settles the preceding interval first.
## Root cause

`applyLiquidityDeltaToPosition()` uses the non-wrap-aware comparison `_blockTimestamp() > _prevTimestamp` even though the `uint32` clock and `_distributeRewards()` use modular elapsed-time semantics.
## Impact

A position owner who enters or exits farming after the timestamp wrap can cause rewards accrued before that change to be allocated using post-change liquidity. Existing participants can be undercredited and newly added liquidity can receive an incorrect share; in the entry sequence described, part of the deducted reward reserve can remain unclaimable by any farm. Exploitation requires an incentive to remain active across the `uint32` timestamp rollover, but does not require privileged access once that condition exists.
## Proof of concept

```
      bonusRewardToken: await context.bonusRewardToken.getAddress(),
      nonce,
    };

    // Create the incentive shortly before the uint32 rollover, then let an existing LP enter
    // exactly seven seconds before wrap. The next public entry occurs after the wrap.
    await time.setNextBlockTimestamp(Number(wrapPoint - preWrapElapsed - 1n));
    await context.eternalFarming.connect(incentiveCreator).createEternalFarming(
      key,
      {
        reward: totalReward,
        bonusReward: 0,
        rewardRate,
        bonusRewardRate: 0,
        minimalPositionWidth: 0,
      },
      await context.pluginObj.getAddress()
    );

    const incentiveId = await context.testIncentiveId.compute(key);
    const incentive = await context.eternalFarming.incentives(incentiveId);
    const virtualPool = new Contract(incentive.virtualPoolAddress, virtualPoolArtifact.abi, ethers.provider);

    await time.setNextBlockTimestamp(Number(wrapPoint - preWrapElapsed));
    await context.farmingCenter.connect(existingLp).enterFarming(key, existingTokenId);
    const initialReserve = (await virtualPool.rewardReserves()).reserve0;
    const existingFarmBefore = await context.eternalFarming.farms(existingTokenId, incentiveId);
    expect(existingFarmBefore.liquidity).to.be.gt(0n);
    expect(await virtualPool.prevTimestamp()).to.equal(wrapPoint - preWrapElapsed);

    await time.setNextBlockTimestamp(Number(wrapPoint + postWrapElapsed));
    await context.farmingCenter.connect(enteringLp).enterFarming(key, enteringTokenId);

    // The vulnerable greater-than guard skipped _distributeRewards(), so the virtual pool still
    // carries the pre-wrap timestamp even though new in-range liquidity has been installed.
    expect(await virtualPool.prevTimestamp()).to.equal(wrapPoint - preWrapElapsed);
    const combinedLiquidity = await virtualPool.currentLiquidity();
    expect(combinedLiquidity).to.be.gt(existingFarmBefore.liquidity);

    await context.farmingCenter.connect(existingLp).collectRewards(key, existingTokenId);
    await context.farmingCenter.connect(enteringLp).collectRewards(key, enteringTokenId);

    const existingReward = await context.eternalFarming.rewards(existingLp.address, await context.rewardToken.getAddress());
    const enteringReward = await context.eternalFarming.rewards(enteringLp.address, await context.rewardToken.getAddress());
    const finalReserve = (await virtualPool.rewardReserves()).reserve0;
    const deducted = initialReserve - finalReserve;

    expect(deducted).to.be.gt(rewardRate * preWrapElapsed);

    // Only the original LP existed during the seven-second pre-wrap interval. A modulo-aware
    // checkpoint before adding the second LP would credit at least that full interval to it, so
    // this assertion is false after the one-line safe fix that settles whenever elapsed != 0.
    expect(existingReward).to.be.lt(rewardRate * preWrapElapsed);

    // The skipped interval is deducted from reserves but neither farm can claim the missing share:
    // the entering farm records its baseline after the hypothetical combined-liquidity growth.
    expect(existingReward + enteringReward).to.be.lt(deducted);
  });
});
```

### Considerations

PoC ran successfully with strategy `unit:cryptoalgebra-integral-farming` using the real `FarmingCenter.enterFarming()`, `AlgebraEternalFarming.enterFarming()/collectRewards()`, and deployed `EternalVirtualPool.applyLiquidityDeltaToPosition()` code. It uses Hardhat time control to place blocks around the uint32 rollover, so it demonstrates the production arithmetic and state transitions in a local VM rather than waiting for wall-clock rollover. The test asserts the vulnerable state that a safe modulo-aware checkpoint would remove: `prevTimestamp` remains pre-wrap after public entry, original LP reward is below the pre-wrap interval it alone supplied, and deducted reserves exceed total claimable rewards.
### Validation reasoning

PoC validation command completed successfully.
## Remediation
### Explanation

Always invoke the existing modulo-aware reward distribution helper before applying a liquidity delta. Its unchecked uint32 subtraction already returns early for same-block calls, while correctly checkpointing elapsed rewards across timestamp rollover.

# Unvalidated immutable dependencies can disable factory operations
**#214916**
- Severity: Low

## Description

`CustomPoolPluginFactory.initialize` accepts any nonzero `factory` and `algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint` address, storing them without verifying deployed code, the required callable interfaces, or their expected relationship. `deployCustomPool` subsequently relies on those references to compute the expected address and create the pool, while owner management functions forward configuration calls through the entry point. The analogous `BasePluginV1Factory` constructor stores `algebraFactory` without validation, although that address controls both `onlyAdministrator` authorization and who may call `createPlugin`. An EOA, an incompatible contract, or mismatched custom-factory endpoint configuration can therefore successfully initialize or construct an instance that fails when its essential cross-contract calls are used. The dependencies have no described replacement path, so validation must occur before committing these operationally immutable references.
## Root cause

Essential external dependency addresses are committed with absent or nonzero-only validation rather than verifying contract code, required interfaces, and required factory/entry-point binding invariants.
## Impact

A bad custom-factory configuration can make pool creation revert and can prevent management operations from reaching the intended entry point. A bad base-factory `algebraFactory` can prevent legitimate plugin creation and administrator-gated operations, leaving the deployed component unusable until it is replaced or upgraded with a recovery mechanism.
## Proof of concept
### Test case

```
import { ethers } from 'hardhat';
import { expect } from './shared/expect';
import { tokensFixture } from './shared/externalFixtures';

import {
  abi as PROXY_ADMIN_ABI,
  bytecode as PROXY_ADMIN_BYTECODE,
} from '@cryptoalgebra/integral-core/artifacts/@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/transparent/ProxyAdmin.sol/ProxyAdmin.json';

const transparentUpgradeableProxyArtifact = require(
  '@cryptoalgebra/integral-core/artifacts/@openzeppelin/contracts/proxy/transparent/' +
    'TransparentUpgradeableProxy.sol/TransparentUpgradeableProxy.json'
);
const { abi: TransparentUpgradeableProxy_ABI, bytecode: TransparentUpgradeableProxy_BYTECODE } = transparentUpgradeableProxyArtifact;

describe('PoC: unvalidated immutable dependency addresses disable plugin factories', () => {
  async function deployCustomPoolPluginFactoryProxy() {
    const customFactoryImplementation = await (await ethers.getContractFactory('CustomPoolPluginFactory')).deploy();
    const proxyAdmin = await (await ethers.getContractFactory(PROXY_ADMIN_ABI, PROXY_ADMIN_BYTECODE)).deploy();
    const customFactoryProxy = await (
      await ethers.getContractFactory(TransparentUpgradeableProxy_ABI, TransparentUpgradeableProxy_BYTECODE)
    ).deploy(customFactoryImplementation.target, proxyAdmin.target, '0x');

    return ethers.getContractAt('CustomPoolPluginFactory', customFactoryProxy.target);
  }

  it('commits non-contract factory/entry-point dependencies and leaves custom-pool deployment unusable', async () => {
    const [deployer, nonContractFactory, nonContractEntryPoint] = await ethers.getSigners();
    const { token0, token1 } = await tokensFixture();
    const token0Address = await token0.getAddress();
    const token1Address = await token1.getAddress();

    const pluginImplementation = await (await ethers.getContractFactory('AlgebraBasePluginV1')).deploy();
    const customFactory = await deployCustomPoolPluginFactoryProxy();

    // The vulnerable initializer accepts EOAs for both operational dependencies.
    await customFactory.initialize(nonContractFactory.address, nonContractEntryPoint.address, pluginImplementation.target);
    expect(await customFactory.factory()).to.eq(nonContractFactory.address);
    expect(await customFactory.algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint()).to.eq(nonContractEntryPoint.address);
    expect(await ethers.provider.getCode(nonContractFactory.address)).to.eq('0x');
    expect(await ethers.provider.getCode(nonContractEntryPoint.address)).to.eq('0x');

    await customFactory.setTokenWhitelistBatch([token0Address, token1Address], true);
    expect(await customFactory.isWhitelistedToken(token0Address)).to.eq(true);
    expect(await customFactory.isWhitelistedToken(token1Address)).to.eq(true);

    // Pool deployment now reaches the real deployCustomPool path and fails at the stored EOA factory call.
    await expect(customFactory.deployCustomPool(token0Address, token1Address, '0x1234')).to.be.reverted;

    // Owner-accessible state remains usable, but the bad operational endpoints are permanently committed.
    await customFactory.setPublicPoolCreationMode(true);
    expect(await customFactory.isPublicPoolCreationMode()).to.eq(true);
    expect(await customFactory.factory()).to.eq(nonContractFactory.address);
    expect(await customFactory.algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint()).to.eq(nonContractEntryPoint.address);

    // Public creation cannot recover: it skips only the deployer role check and still dereferences the bad factory.
    await expect(customFactory.connect(nonContractFactory).deployCustomPool(token0Address, token1Address, '0xbeef')).to.be.reverted;
    expect(await customFactory.pluginByPool(deployer.address)).to.eq(ethers.ZeroAddress);
  });

  it('constructs a base plugin factory with a non-contract algebraFactory and disables administrator operations', async () => {
    const [deployer, nonContractFactory, newFarmingAddress] = await ethers.getSigners();
    const pluginImplementation = await (await ethers.getContractFactory('AlgebraBasePluginV1')).deploy();
    const baseFactory = await (await ethers.getContractFactory('BasePluginV1Factory')).deploy(nonContractFactory.address, pluginImplementation.target);

    // The vulnerable constructor accepts and immutably stores an EOA as the authorization factory.
    expect(await baseFactory.algebraFactory()).to.eq(nonContractFactory.address);
    expect(await ethers.provider.getCode(nonContractFactory.address)).to.eq('0x');
    expect(await baseFactory.farmingAddress()).to.eq(ethers.ZeroAddress);

    // Real administrator-gated functions cannot authorize anyone because onlyAdministrator calls the EOA as IAlgebraFactory.
    await expect(baseFactory.connect(deployer).setFarmingAddress(newFarmingAddress.address)).to.be.reverted;
    await expect(baseFactory.connect(nonContractFactory).setFarmingAddress(newFarmingAddress.address)).to.be.reverted;
    expect(await baseFactory.farmingAddress()).to.eq(ethers.ZeroAddress);

    await expect(baseFactory.connect(deployer).upgradeTo(pluginImplementation.target)).to.be.reverted;
    expect(await baseFactory.implementation()).to.eq(await pluginImplementation.getAddress());
  });
});
```

## Remediation
### Explanation

Validate both operational factory dependencies as deployed contracts implementing the authorization interface, and validate that the custom entry point is deployed and bound to the same Algebra factory before storing immutable configuration.

```diff
+    require(IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(_algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).factory() == _factory, 'Invalid entry point');

     defaultFeeConfiguration = AdaptiveFee.initialFeeConfiguration();
 
     _grantRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, msg.sender);

   /// @notice Deploys a custom pool with a newly created default plugin.

   /// @return customPool The newly created custom pool.
   function deployCustomPool(address tokenA, address tokenB, bytes calldata data) external returns (address customPool) {
     if (!isPublicPoolCreationMode) {
       _checkRole(CUSTOM_POOL_DEPLOYER);
     }
     require(isWhitelistedToken[tokenA], 'TokenA not whitelisted');
     require(isWhitelistedToken[tokenB], 'TokenB not whitelisted');
 
     (address token0, address token1) = _sortTokens(tokenA, tokenB);
     address expectedPool = IAlgebraFactory(factory).computeCustomPoolAddress(address(this), token0, token1);
     require(_pendingCustomPoolByAddress[expectedPool].creator == address(0), 'Pool creation pending');
 
     _pendingCustomPoolByAddress[expectedPool] = PendingCustomPool({
       creator: msg.sender,
       token0: token0,
       token1: token1,
       plugin: address(0),
       dataHash: keccak256(data)
     });
 
     customPool = IAlgebraCustomPoolEntryPoint(algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint).createCustomPool(address(this), msg.sender, tokenA, tokenB, data);

     require(msg.sender == algebraCustomPoolEntryPoint, 'Only entry point');
     require(deployer == address(this), 'Invalid deployer');

     require(pendingCustomPool.creator == creator, 'Invalid creator');
     require(pendingCustomPool.token0 == token0 && pendingCustomPool.token1 == token1, 'Invalid tokens');
     require(pendingCustomPool.dataHash == keccak256(data), 'Invalid data');
 
     plugin = _createPlugin(pool);

   }
 
   /// @inheritdoc IAlgebraPluginFactory
   function afterCreatePoolHook(address plugin, address pool, address deployer) external override {

     require(pendingCustomPool.creator != address(0), 'Pool not pending');

     defaultFeeConfiguration = newConfig;
     emit DefaultFeeConfiguration(newConfig);
   }
 
   /// @notice Upgrades the beacon to a new implementation.
   function upgradeTo(address newImplementation) external onlyOwner {
     _setImplementation(newImplementation);
   }
 
   function _createPlugin(address pool) internal returns (address plugin) {
     require(pluginByPool[pool] == address(0), 'Already created');
     IAlgebraBasePluginV1 customPoolPlugin = IAlgebraBasePluginV1(address(new BeaconProxy(address(this), '')));
     customPoolPlugin.initialize(pool, factory, address(this));
     customPoolPlugin.changeFeeConfiguration(defaultFeeConfiguration);
     plugin = address(customPoolPlugin);
     pluginByPool[pool] = plugin;
   }
 
   function _setTokenWhitelist(address token, bool allowed) internal {

     require(isWhitelistedToken[token] != allowed);

   function _setImplementation(address newImplementation) internal {
     if (newImplementation.code.length == 0) {

   /// @dev Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account.

     super._transferOwnership(newOwner);
     if (owner() != address(0)) {
       _grantRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, owner());
     }
   }
 
   uint256[50] private __gap;
```

# Malformed token symbols can revert position metadata reads
**#214935**
- Severity: Low
- Validity: Unreviewed
## Source locations
### `src/periphery/contracts/libraries/SafeERC20Namer.sol` (2 locations)
#### Lines 60-75 — _Successful returndata longer than 64 bytes is decoded as a string without structural validation or a try/catch._

```
    // calls an external view token contract method that returns a symbol or name, and parses the output into a string
    function callAndParseStringReturn(address token, bytes4 selector) private view returns (string memory) {
        (bool success, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(selector));
        // if not implemented, or returns empty data, return empty string
        if (!success || data.length == 0) {
            return '';
        }
        // bytes32 data always has length 32
        if (data.length == 32) {
            bytes32 decoded = abi.decode(data, (bytes32));
            return bytes32ToString(decoded);
        } else if (data.length > 64) {
            return abi.decode(data, (string));
        }
        return '';
    }
```
⋯
#### Lines 77-85 — _`tokenSymbol` uses the parser for metadata displayed by the descriptor._

```
    // attempts to extract the token symbol. if it does not implement symbol, returns a symbol derived from the address
    function tokenSymbol(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {
        // 0x95d89b41 = bytes4(keccak256("symbol()"))
        string memory symbol = callAndParseStringReturn(token, 0x95d89b41);
        if (bytes(symbol).length == 0) {
            // fallback to 6 uppercase hex of address
            return addressToSymbol(token);
        }
        return symbol;
```
### `src/periphery/contracts/NonfungibleTokenPositionDescriptor.sol`
#### Lines 82-95 — _Both token symbols are obtained during `tokenURI` construction._ — _The descriptor uses the symbol helper for both non-native token symbols._

```
        return
            NFTDescriptor.constructTokenURI(
                NFTDescriptor.ConstructTokenURIParams({
                    tokenId: tokenId,
                    quoteTokenAddress: quoteTokenAddress,
                    baseTokenAddress: baseTokenAddress,
                    quoteTokenSymbol: quoteTokenAddress == WNativeToken
                        ? nativeCurrencySymbol()
                        : SafeERC20Namer.tokenSymbol(quoteTokenAddress),
                    baseTokenSymbol: baseTokenAddress == WNativeToken
                        ? nativeCurrencySymbol()
                        : SafeERC20Namer.tokenSymbol(baseTokenAddress),
                    quoteTokenDecimals: IERC20Metadata(quoteTokenAddress).decimals(),
                    baseTokenDecimals: IERC20Metadata(baseTokenAddress).decimals(),
```
## Description

`callAndParseStringReturn` treats every successful `symbol()` response longer than `64` bytes as an ABI-encoded `string` and invokes `abi.decode(data, (string))`. A token can successfully return malformed dynamic ABI data, including an invalid offset or length, that causes this decode to revert. The revert bypasses `tokenSymbol`'s address-derived fallback because that fallback only runs after the parser returns an empty string. `NonfungibleTokenPositionDescriptor.tokenURI` resolves both non-native pool-token symbols through this path, so the malformed response reaches a public metadata read. The parser should reject or safely handle malformed dynamic return data and return an empty value so the existing fallback can be used.
## Root cause

`callAndParseStringReturn` assumes successful returndata longer than `64` bytes is a valid ABI-encoded `string` and lets `abi.decode` failures escape instead of converting them to the empty-value fallback.
## Impact

A malformed or nonconforming token included in a pool can cause `tokenURI` to revert for every position NFT associated with that pool. Indexers, marketplaces, and user interfaces may be unable to retrieve the affected metadata, but this path does not alter position accounting or transfer underlying assets.
## Proof of concept
### Test case

```
import { MaxUint256, ZeroAddress } from 'ethers';
import { ethers } from 'hardhat';
import { loadFixture } from '@nomicfoundation/hardhat-network-helpers';

import completeFixture from './shared/completeFixture';
import { FeeAmount, TICK_SPACINGS } from './shared/constants';
import { encodePriceSqrt } from './shared/encodePriceSqrt';
import { expect } from './shared/expect';
import { getMaxTick, getMinTick } from './shared/ticks';

describe('PoC: malformed token symbols can revert position metadata reads', function () {
  this.timeout(40_000);

  it('mints a real position, then tokenURI reverts when SafeERC20Namer decodes malformed symbol returndata', async () => {
    const [owner] = await ethers.getSigners();
    const { factory, nft } = await loadFixture(completeFixture);

    const malformedFactory = await ethers.getContractFactory('MalformedSymbolERC20');
    const regularFactory = await ethers.getContractFactory('TestERC20');
    const malformedToken = await malformedFactory.deploy(MaxUint256 / 2n);
    const regularToken = await regularFactory.deploy(MaxUint256 / 2n);

    const malformedAddress = await malformedToken.getAddress();
    const regularAddress = await regularToken.getAddress();

    const rawSymbolReturndata = await ethers.provider.call({ to: malformedAddress, data: '0x95d89b41' });
    expect((rawSymbolReturndata.length - 2) / 2).to.equal(96);

    const sortedTokens = [
      { contract: malformedToken, address: malformedAddress },
      { contract: regularToken, address: regularAddress },
    ].sort((a, b) => (a.address.toLowerCase() < b.address.toLowerCase() ? -1 : 1));
    const [token0, token1] = sortedTokens;

    await token0.contract.approve(await nft.getAddress(), MaxUint256);
    await token1.contract.approve(await nft.getAddress(), MaxUint256);

    await nft.createAndInitializePoolIfNecessary(token0.address, token1.address, encodePriceSqrt(1, 1));
    const poolAddress = await factory.poolByPair(token0.address, token1.address);
    expect(poolAddress).to.not.equal(ZeroAddress);

    await nft.mint({
      token0: token0.address,
      token1: token1.address,
      deployer: ZeroAddress,
      tickLower: getMinTick(TICK_SPACINGS[FeeAmount.MEDIUM]),
      tickUpper: getMaxTick(TICK_SPACINGS[FeeAmount.MEDIUM]),
      amount0Desired: 1_000_000,
      amount1Desired: 1_000_000,
      amount0Min: 0,
      amount1Min: 0,
      recipient: owner.address,
      deadline: 1,
    });

    const position = await nft.positions(1);
    expect(await nft.ownerOf(1)).to.equal(owner.address);
    expect(position.liquidity).to.be.gt(0);

    await expect(nft.tokenURI(1)).to.be.reverted;
  });
});
```

### Considerations

PoC compiles and passes in the periphery Hardhat harness. It demonstrates the claimed metadata-read DoS only: a real NonfungiblePositionManager position is minted through public entry points, and the public tokenURI read reverts when the descriptor reaches SafeERC20Namer.tokenSymbol for a token whose symbol() succeeds with malformed dynamic returndata. It does not demonstrate asset loss or position-accounting corruption.
### Validation reasoning

PoC validation command completed successfully.
## Remediation
### Explanation

Validate the dynamic ABI string offset and declared/padded length before parsing token symbol/name returndata; malformed successful responses now return empty so the existing address-derived fallback is used without changing valid bytes32 or string behavior.
### Patch

```diff
diff --git a/src/periphery/contracts/libraries/SafeERC20Namer.sol b/src/periphery/contracts/libraries/SafeERC20Namer.sol
--- a/src/periphery/contracts/libraries/SafeERC20Namer.sol
+++ b/src/periphery/contracts/libraries/SafeERC20Namer.sol
@@ -1,98 +1,108 @@
 // SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
 
 pragma solidity >=0.8.0;
 
 import './AddressStringUtil.sol';
 
 // produces token descriptors from inconsistent or absent ERC20 symbol implementations that can return string or bytes32
 // this library will always produce a string symbol to represent the token
 library SafeERC20Namer {
     function bytes32ToString(bytes32 x) private pure returns (string memory) {
         unchecked {
             bytes memory bytesString = new bytes(32);
             uint256 charCount = 0;
             for (uint256 j = 0; j < 32; j++) {
                 bytes1 char = x[j];
                 if (char != 0) {
                     bytesString[charCount] = char;
                     charCount++;
                 }
             }
             bytes memory bytesStringTrimmed = new bytes(charCount);
             for (uint256 j = 0; j < charCount; j++) {
                 bytesStringTrimmed[j] = bytesString[j];
             }
             return string(bytesStringTrimmed);
         }
     }
 
     // assumes the data is in position 2
     function parseStringData(bytes memory b) private pure returns (string memory) {
         unchecked {
             uint256 charCount = 0;
             // first parse the charCount out of the data
             for (uint256 i = 32; i < 64; i++) {
                 charCount <<= 8;
                 charCount += uint8(b[i]);
             }
 
             bytes memory bytesStringTrimmed = new bytes(charCount);
             for (uint256 i = 0; i < charCount; i++) {
                 bytesStringTrimmed[i] = b[i + 64];
             }
 
             return string(bytesStringTrimmed);
         }
     }
 
     // uses a heuristic to produce a token name from the address
     // the heuristic returns the full hex of the address string in upper case
     function addressToName(address token) private pure returns (string memory) {
         return AddressStringUtil.toAsciiString(token, 40);
     }
 
     // uses a heuristic to produce a token symbol from the address
     // the heuristic returns the first 6 hex of the address string in upper case
     function addressToSymbol(address token) private pure returns (string memory) {
         return AddressStringUtil.toAsciiString(token, 6);
     }
 
     // calls an external view token contract method that returns a symbol or name, and parses the output into a string
     function callAndParseStringReturn(address token, bytes4 selector) private view returns (string memory) {
         (bool success, bytes memory data) = token.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(selector));
         // if not implemented, or returns empty data, return empty string
         if (!success || data.length == 0) {
             return '';
         }
         // bytes32 data always has length 32
         if (data.length == 32) {
             bytes32 decoded = abi.decode(data, (bytes32));
             return bytes32ToString(decoded);
         } else if (data.length > 64) {
-            return abi.decode(data, (string));
+            uint256 offset;
+            uint256 stringLength;
+            assembly {
+                offset := mload(add(data, 32))
+                stringLength := mload(add(data, 64))
+            }
+            // A single ABI-encoded string has a 32-byte offset followed by its length and padded data.
+            if (offset != 32 || stringLength > data.length - 64) return '';
+            uint256 paddedStringLength = (stringLength + 31) & ~uint256(31);
+            if (paddedStringLength > data.length - 64) return '';
+            return parseStringData(data);
         }
         return '';
     }
 
     // attempts to extract the token symbol. if it does not implement symbol, returns a symbol derived from the address
     function tokenSymbol(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {
         // 0x95d89b41 = bytes4(keccak256("symbol()"))
         string memory symbol = callAndParseStringReturn(token, 0x95d89b41);
         if (bytes(symbol).length == 0) {
             // fallback to 6 uppercase hex of address
             return addressToSymbol(token);
         }
         return symbol;
     }
 
     // attempts to extract the token name. if it does not implement name, returns a name derived from the address
     function tokenName(address token) internal view returns (string memory) {
         // 0x06fdde03 = bytes4(keccak256("name()"))
         string memory name = callAndParseStringReturn(token, 0x06fdde03);
         if (bytes(name).length == 0) {
             // fallback to full hex of address
             return addressToName(token);
         }
         return name;
     }
 }
```

- `src/periphery/contracts/libraries/SafeERC20Namer.sol`
